rationale: Scotia Wind is an underlying development project of Circle Power Renewables, not a separate manager-level Amber portfolio company. Amber's current energy-investment page identifies Circle Power Renewables as its U.S. investment, while the Hunt launch announcement expressly describes Scotia Wind as the joint venture's first project. Consolidate the project record into the platform, preserve its historical ownership and milestones, remove the dead project-domain citation, and keep one active Amber ownership period at the platform level.

acquisitionExitCheck.acquisitionSearch: Amber and Circle Power launched Circle Power Renewables on May 27, 2021 as a renewable development platform; their announcement identifies Scotia Wind as the pre-existing joint venture's first project.
acquisitionExitCheck.exitSearch: No Amber exit from Circle Power Renewables was found. Amber's current energy page still describes investing in Circle Power Renewables in the United States.
acquisitionExitCheck.currentProjectStatus: The Scotia Wind project domain no longer resolves, Circle Power's current website does not present Scotia Wind as a standalone business, and current evidence continues to support the platform—not the project—as the manager-level company boundary. Project-specific permitting outcomes do not create a separate PortCo identity.
